title: 3rd Sitting of 1st Session of 2025
presiding: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim (opening and question time); Abdul Gafoor Moosa (Hanimaadhoo) took the chair after the 10:29-11:01 break
summary: The sitting opened at 09:00 with 28 members present, 3 on leave and 11 on official travel. Twelve members put questions to the Minister of Fisheries and Ocean Resources, Ahmed Shiyam, on fish prices, MIFCO purchasing, ice plants, a kanneli packing facility at Hulhumale, sports-fishing buoys and prompt payment to fishers. Six presidential nominations (ambassadors and a vice-president of the Anti-Corruption Commission) and a Rules of Procedure amendment were sent to committees. After a break, the government's bill amending the Decentralisation Act to clarify the role of Women's Development Committees and give members a Ramadan allowance was debated, mostly by supporters; the debate was still under way when this part ends and no vote was taken. This part continues the debate on a government bill to amend the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) so that members of Women's Development Committees (WDCs) get a proper allowance, including a Ramadan allowance. Six members spoke after a speech that began in the previous part; most welcomed the bill, with exchanges over whether the WDC system was created by the MDP or grew out of earlier community structures, and some asked committee to check for double allowances and how WDCs work with island councils. After a recess the bill's sponsor wound up the debate and the Majlis voted 59-0 to accept it and send it to the Decentralisation Committee. The chair then closed the sitting until Wednesday 12 February 2025 at 9:00. The text is partly garbled, so speaker gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shiyam
positions: As Minister of Fisheries and Ocean Resources, answered questions on fish prices, MIFCO purchasing, ice plants, boats and payment to fishers within 48 hours.
Said a kanneli packing facility at Hulhumale has funding and work could start in about two months, with a mid-year target.
Said sports-fishing buoy networks, India-funded projects and Addu Fisheries Complex expansion are being advanced.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked what the government is doing to secure steady incomes for fishers and fish processors, and why some fishers get no subsidy.
Asked when the presidential pledge on kanneli prices (MVR 80 to 100) would start.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when the pledge for MIFCO to buy kanneli would be put into practice, and how long fixing ice plant problems would take.

Welcomed good changes for WDCs but disputed the earlier speaker's account, saying the WDC system and first allowances came under the MDP-era system, and said his party would vote for beneficial changes.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Asked what is being done about rules that limit foreign workers on the smaller fishing boats used from Malé.
Spoke in the bill debate; said the amendments give Women's Development Committee members pay, leave and Ramadan allowance and criticised earlier governments' handling of them.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked about action against illegal fishing, the 48-hour payment policy, and when a fish collection boat would serve Fuvahmulah.
In the bill debate, supported the amendments and said they give Women's Development Committee members fuller powers and allowances.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked how much previous governments left unpaid to fishers and how sports-fishing buoys are progressing.
In the bill debate, welcomed the Ramadan allowance and pay provisions for Women's Development Committee members.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when the fish price would be changed to the pledged level and when Addu Fisheries Complex expansion would start.
Supported the bill but worried members who already hold other state posts might receive a double allowance, and asked committee to check this.
Said paying the allowance as a salary into accounts helps members use loans and credit.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked what benefit fishers have received from the China free trade agreement, and about bank financing for freelance sports-fishing workers.
Agreed with the main points but said WDC and council relations differ island by island and the rules, including the 33% women's seats, need wider review.
Asked whether the Ramadan allowance should go only to WDC members or also to others, and urged committee to study this.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: As sponsor, said the bill clarifies the mandate of Women's Development Committees, their funding, advisory role and Ramadan allowance.
As the bill's sponsor, said the bill sets rules for handing assets to councils and creates a framework for the National Pay Commission to set WDC pay on local government advice.
Said it also gives a Ramadan allowance to WDC members who do not get one under another law.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when the kanneli packing facility being built at Hulhumale would start and finish.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when the ice plant at Thulhaadhoo, whose service has stopped, would resume operating.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked when work on the stalled ice plant in his constituency would start and finish.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked about the effect of the price change for smaller fish, long waits at the fish queue, and progress on expanding the Addu Fisheries Complex.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked about the stalled Lhohi ice plant and sought sports-fishing buoys for Foddhoo.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Welcomed the amendments, said members would get a Ramadan allowance of MVR 3,000 from this year, and thanked the President.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill and called for the Ramadan allowance to reach all workers, including private-sector employees.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Supported the bill, saying it makes the committees' mandate clearer and thanked the government and the sponsor.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, noted no MDP members were in the chamber, and argued the state should reduce spending.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the bill, noting the law had no amendment in about 15 years and the Ramadan allowance is set at MVR 3,000.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Welcomed the amendments and said the law now obliges Ramadan allowance for Women's Development Committee members.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill, defended the President's island visits, and cited recent council election results; speech continues past end of this part.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said women's development committees were not created by any party, and that the decentralisation law has been amended more than any other.
Argued the amendment gives WDC members state allowances and would end repeated WDC elections, saving public money.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Rejected the claim that the MDP created the WDCs, saying the committees existed on islands for long before.
Described the amendment's changes to the allowance clauses and welcomed the Ramadan allowance for WDC members.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the amendment, saying paying the allowance as salary eases access to loans and credit cards and the Ramadan allowance meets a presidential pledge.
Said island councils should not obstruct government projects such as ATMs on islands, and that the law should allow action against those that do.

decisions: Minutes of the first to third special sittings held outside the 2025 term were declared accepted, as no corrections were proposed.
The ambassador nominations for the IMO, IRENA, WTO, Canada and Egypt posts were sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The Anti-Corruption Commission vice-president nomination was sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The Rules of Procedure amendment from the North Galolhu member was sent to the General Committee.
Debate on the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) amendment bill ended after the sponsor's closing remarks.
The Majlis accepted the bill 59-0 and sent it to the Decentralisation Committee under rule 106(r).
Sitting closed; next sitting Wednesday 12 February 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to amend the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010), sponsored by Ahmed Xamyr (Central Mahchangolhi)
